prompt: Some people think it is a good thing for senior managers to have much higher salaries than other workers in a company. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Many argue that giving senior managers higher salaries than other employees is beneficial, while others believe otherwise. I totally believe that paying senior managers more is reasonable because they have heavier responsibilities and generally work for longer hours.

One primary reason why it is a good thing for senior managers to be paid more is that they usually have more work and duties than regular employees. They may need to lead a whole group of people in a meeting, go on business trips, or have more paperwork. They typically have more responsibilities than regular employees do. Therefore, all the additional work is time-consuming and tiring. To illustrate, as a senior manager myself, I often lead meetings daily and sacrifice my weekends going on business trips. As a result, having higher salaries is reasonable because senior managers need to dedicate much more time to their work.

Furthermore, with more responsibilities and time consumption, if senior directors were to be paid the same amount as ordinary workers, it would not be fair to them. This would make the managers have a feeling that they are not getting back what they worked for, which could lead to being less motivated when working. To illustrate, I once knew a friend who was a senior manager, and he eventually quit his job because the amount of money he was receiving from the company he was working for was not identical to the amount of work and time he put in.

In conclusion, I completely agree with giving senior managers higher salaries because their job is more difficult and requires more working time. Therefore, given the situation, senior managers should be paid more than other workers.
